di_rare_metals_com_o2_o5_o1_s1.proposition: Taken together, the earlier XRD/DSC result (a distinct compound detected only in the La alloy, not the Sm alloy) and the morphology observation (interdendritic phase ranges from a continuous network to isolated particles to thin broken strings across the panels) support that the compositional difference distinguishing La from Sm co-occurs with the microstructural difference distinguishing La from Sm: the alloy in which a new, distinct phase was structurally and thermally detected (La) is also the alloy showing the more fragmented, more discontinuous interdendritic morphology, consistent with La producing a stronger break-up of the network than Sm.
limits: The pairing only shows that phase-detection and morphology-refinement track together across the same alloys; it does not establish that the newly detected La compound is the mechanistic cause of the finer/more discontinuous morphology

Neither piece quantifies the new phase (only presence/absence of its signatures) nor quantifies the morphology change (only qualitative descriptors of network continuity), so no dose-response or amount-based link between phase content and degree of fragmentation can be drawn

The identity of the new phase itself is not derived from this pairing (per the earlier result's qualification), so any morphological role attributed to 'the new compound' rests on an unverified identity

Absence of detected new-phase signatures in Sm does not prove none formed (detection-limit caveat carries over), so the apparent link between phase presence and lesser fragmentation in Sm could instead reflect an undetected phase still influencing morphology
di_rare_metals_com_o2_o5_o1_s1.not_identifiable: Whether the new La-specific compound formation is what drives the greater interdendritic fragmentation in La versus Sm, or whether the fragmentation instead arises from other RE-related alloying effects (e.g., interface/segregation effects) that happen to co-occur with, but are not caused by, the detected compound
